name: Data Converter
description: Convert anything in one DBX workbench panel: 13 formats (JSON / YAML / XML / Properties / TOML / INI / .env / CSV / TSV / Query / Headers / Cookie / HTML) in any combination, JSONPath / jq queries with JSON Schema validation, eight escape tools (URL / Base64 / HTML / JSON / Unicode / Hex / SQL / Regex), batch text to SQL (IN / NOT IN / INSERT), .xlsx / .csv / .tsv to JSON, Image ⇄ Base64, and a Byte Converter (B/KB/MB/GB/TB/PB on both the 1000 and 1024 scales, exact ⇄ human readable, batch totals, plus hex dump / byte array / binary string). A Code Gen page turns a JSON sample or a CREATE TABLE into TypeScript / Go / Java / Python models, and a Chart page renders an ECharts option (or bare numbers) as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with custom width and height, exported as PNG or SVG. Pure frontend, no backend, works offline.
releaseNotes: 0.1.6 (update): a new Chart page renders an ECharts option — or just an array of numbers — as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with an editable width and height (80 to 4096), exported as PNG (1:1 pixels) or SVG (vector text, via renderToSVGString). Line / bar / area / pie / scatter and every other ECharts type work, and a full option decides its own chart type. Real API responses work as they are: an option buried under a business key as a string ({"monthly_trend":{"echart_option":"{…}"}}) is unwrapped automatically and the status line says which key it came from, several charts in one JSON get a picker, and one JSON per line (NDJSON) or back-to-back objects are split into separate charts. The preview is drawn at exactly the pixels you typed and never stretched. The ECharts 6.1.0 engine (Apache-2.0) ships inside the package, is only loaded when you open that page, and is released when you leave it. Every dead end is explained — bad JSON with a line number, an unrecognised shape, too many points or series, an engine that failed to load — instead of leaving you with a blank canvas. A full option can also have its type overridden from the toolbar (Auto keeps what the JSON says), and the engine now loads through a blob URL handed back by the host, so it works inside the DBX sandbox where an external script tag is blocked by CSP. Large canvases now fit the pane automatically, with −/Fit/percentage/+ controls to inspect real pixels (zoom only changes the view — exports keep the exact pixels you typed), and the Image ⇄ Base64 preview uses the same controls without ever stretching the picture. All ten pages are translated into 14 languages, and everything runs locally: no network, no eval. The new Pixel ratio control (1x / 2x / 3x) sets the render-time devicePixelRatio, so the same 700 x 400 chart exports at 700x400, 1400x800 or 2100x1200 — each option states the pixels it yields and the file name gets an @2x / @3x suffix. Zoom in (or double-click the canvas) opens the chart in a full-screen lightbox that renders at that same ratio, and every save now reports what actually happened (saved, downloaded, cancelled or failed) instead of always claiming success.
